summary: Verified fix for React StrictMode 'destroy is not a function' overlay on policy pages. Tested /terms, /refund-policy, /shipping-policy via direct navigation AND footer link clicks (footer-terms, footer-refund, footer-shipping). Explicitly listened for page.on('pageerror') and inspected #webpack-dev-server-client-overlay iframe content. Result: 0 pageerrors, 0 console errors, 0 overlay visible on all 3 policy pages. Regression on /, /shop, /product/:id, /cart, /checkout also clean.
critical_code_review_comments: PolicyLayout.jsx useEffect now correctly uses block body — fix is sound. Consider adopting a lint rule (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps + no-implicit-return in effects) to prevent regressions of implicit-return useEffect callbacks elsewhere.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified. PolicyLayout.jsx line 9-11 uses block-body useEffect. All 3 policy routes render cleanly with no CRA error overlay. Test methodology: page.on('pageerror'), inspect iframe#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay content_frame body text for verification.
rca of the issue: React 18 StrictMode invokes effect cleanup during dev mount. Arrow function `useEffect(() => window.scrollTo(0,0), [])` implicitly returns the value of window.scrollTo (undefined at runtime, but in some codepaths React treats the non-function return value strictly and throws 'destroy is not a function' when attempting to invoke the returned cleanup). Fix: wrap body in braces so the arrow returns undefined explicitly. Verified via Playwright with pageerror listener + CRA overlay iframe inspection.
